page: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-intensive server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system features 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, but includes a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 300,543.62 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 989.01 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached small-block reads at 14,555.46 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 860.6 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, with Redis achieving 355.04 million operations per second.

While multi-core and memory-bound operations perform in the top tier, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Additionally, LLM text generation speeds are limited, with the 135M model achieving a poor rating of 16.66 tokens per second. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture and high DDR5 memory density offer high resource consolidation for memory-bound workloads, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage solutions.

This server is designed for large-scale memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, large-scale software compilation, and high-concurrency web serving.
